selection.worker_obligation: re-measure BOTH the container sha256 and the decompressed-content sha256 before any successful real-data result, and STOP on mismatch. no measurement may silently promote a different file.

what_this_is: The MEASURED identity of the corpus bytes selected as the bounded Path E pilot corpus, plus the provenance that was verified for them. Manager selected these bytes by durable decision D-20260908-PATH-E-PILOT-CORPUS-SELECTED (GitHub Issue #1 comment 5592977288), under the Captain-approved Path E strategy. It was a PROPOSAL until that decision; it is now a recorded operational selection.
what_this_is_not: Not global corpus authority, not a ratified MTG semantic ruling, not codebook authority, and not permission to replace the corpus with a newer download. `ratified` stays false ON PURPOSE: the selecting decision states in its own words that it is an operational input selection and not a semantic ratification. docs/codebook-authority.json remains the ratified selector for the CODEBOOK; the corpus still has no counterpart, and the selecting decision explicitly declines to require one for the pilot.

corpus.path_is: repository-relative; resolved against the runtime's explicit --root
corpus.content_sha256_is: sha256 of the DECOMPRESSED bytes. a gzip header carries an mtime field, so two containers holding identical data have different file digests; this is the digest that survives recompression and the one that matches the archive
corpus.format: Scryfall oracle-cards bulk data, gzip JSONL, one card record per line

provenance.declared_corpus_ref_source: docs/codebook-authority.json corpus_ref, and every assertion corpus_ref in the selected codebook. it is a SNAPSHOT LABEL, not a byte identity

archived_copy.measured_container_difference: the two containers are the same length and differ at exactly three byte offsets -- 4, 5 and 6 -- which is the gzip header MTIME field. every other byte of both files is identical, and the decompressed streams hash to the same value
archived_copy.how_verified: read-only rclone copy of the archived object into a scratch directory outside the repository, then a full byte comparison and two digests. no repository byte was written and the archive was not modified

corroboration.note: data/artifacts/manifest.json records 38,233 cards for snapshot version 2026-07-04, and this corpus loads 38,233 unique oracle_ids. that is CONSISTENCY, not byte-pinning: the manifest was produced from this same corpus, so it corroborates the snapshot label and cannot certify bytes

review_required: the corpus identity itself is SELECTED and no longer awaits ratification; what remains open is whether the corpus deserves a tracked selector of its own, as the codebook has. the selecting decision leaves that open and does not require it for the pilot.
